speaker: thomas_pope
text: Sit. The meat is on the board. I am not waiting on a man who has been across the water.

speaker: agnes_tipping
text: Sit when you are sat. I have a room of men and one dinner. I am not running a second for a man on the bridge.

speaker: john_heminges
text: He said he would come. We are due at the house by the second bell. Eat.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am in it at two. That is the whole of my news. I am not naming the part at a table.

speaker: will_kemp
text: You are full of news you will not spend. Where is Raye.

speaker: hired_men
text: Here. I have been across the water. I paid Master Henslowe twelve pence on my debt, and I saw it written down.

speaker: john_heminges
text: Twelve pence. On your debt, not on ours. Say the rest before Will turns it into a proverb.

speaker: hired_men
text: He has yesterday's play set against the thirtieth. I saw the page. By Master Henslowe's book, today is the thirty-first of April.

speaker: will_kemp
text: The thirty-first. Then he owes me a day's wage for a day he invented. I will take it in coin.

speaker: thomas_pope
text: Or we play twice on it. A day that is not a day can hold two houses.

speaker: john_heminges
text: Thomas. I have never misdated a line in my life. Were the sums at least right.

speaker: hired_men
text: To the farthing.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then he knows what matters. A man may lose a day. Nobody loses a shilling by mistake.

speaker: will_kemp
text: On the thirty-first of April. That is when a thing will not happen. I shall be rich on it, which is how I know it is never.

speaker: thomas_pope
text: On the thirty-first of April, then. I shall be paid double, and the river shall be dry.

speaker: john_heminges
text: The phrase is enough. On the thirty-first of April. I am not opening a second book for a joke.

speaker: will_kemp
text: I'll sell him a thirty-second of May for sixpence. He may date it how he likes.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Sixpence for a day that is not a month either. Keep your offer. The phrase is the pay.

speaker: hired_men
text: I brought no sum of his house. Twelve pence on my debt is what I saw written. Yesterday's play was Long Meg. I am not telling you what the yard paid him.

speaker: john_heminges
text: Good. Do not. No sum of that house at this table.

speaker: agnes_tipping
text: Then pay me for the dinner you are eating, and not for a day that is not on my slate.

speaker: thomas_pope
text: Long Meg, and a date that is not a date. I can eat to that.

speaker: will_kemp
text: I wanted the extra day in coin, and I have been paid in a proverb.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: You have been given the company's word for never. Use it when you mean never. Do not use it when you mean sixpence.

speaker: will_kemp
text: On the thirty-first of April I shall be brief.

speaker: john_heminges
text: You will not be brief. Eat. Two of the clock, and Will is in the Shrew. I am not discussing the part.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: There is no king on this table. The leaf is at home. It stays at home.

speaker: thomas_pope
text: Then the leaf is wiser than the dinner. A man may lose a day. I am not losing the meat.

speaker: hired_men
text: Henslowe has his twelve pence. I have the page in my head, and I am not going back across the water for a better one.

speaker: will_kemp
text: If you do go back, buy me the thirty-second. Sixpence. I can wait until the thirty-first.

speaker: john_heminges
text: You will wait longer than that. Saturday is a real share. Today is a dinner.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Saturday is Saturday. Today I am in the play, and then I am home. John, you hated the date. You liked the farthing.

speaker: john_heminges
text: I liked the farthing. A farthing wrong is a man who cannot count. A day wrong is a man in a hurry.

speaker: thomas_pope
text: He may lose his days. He does not hold our shillings.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: He does not hold them. Nobody loses a shilling by mistake.

speaker: agnes_tipping
text: Then the phrase can leave with you. My slate cannot. Eat, and go to your bell.
